Apple is reported to have been working with LG to develop "second-party" Home accessories, but new leaks suggest that another company will also be launching "second-party" smart home products.

iOS 27.2 code reveals that non-LG "second-party" new Home accessories are on the way

Over the past day, we have seen multiple leaks about Apple's ambitions to expand its smart home ecosystem.

In addition to its own Home products expected to launch next week, such as the new Apple TV 4K, "HomePad", and HomePod mini 2, the company is also reportedly working with LG to develop a new range of home accessories.

These accessories are co-developed by Apple and LG but will be sold under the LG brand. Today's leaked images have revealed what they look like:

  • Leaked images reveal Apple-developed smart door locks, thermostats, and more for LG
  • Leaked images show Apple-designed Home cameras and doorbells for LG

It makes perfect sense for Apple to bolster its smart home ecosystem by co-developing products. It turns out this partnership may not be limited to LG alone.

Leaker pdfu has found evidence in iOS 27.2 of two additional Home accessories labelled as "second-party".

These accessories are a Schneider-branded smart thermostat and a temperature and humidity sensor.

As pdfu's post pointed out, currently in Apple's HomeKit database, only these new LG accessories and the two aforementioned Schneider products carry the "second-party" label.

By being classified as second-party, these accessories will "receive special treatment from the operating system".

It is currently unclear whether this means Apple is working as closely with Schneider to develop accessories, as it is reportedly doing with LG. But that is certainly the direction the code suggests.

What do you think of Apple's reported new Home product strategy? Let us know in the comments.
